page: Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is a key component of this instance, featuring 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with the server placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, achieving top 25% performance in both small-block cached reads at 6697.62 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 338.82 GB/sec. The processor's extended instruction capabilities are reflected in top 10% tier results for Passmark CPU extended instructions, encryption tests, ray tracing, and image processing.

Given its bare-metal architecture, high-density local NVMe storage, and substantial memory capacity, the i4i.metal offers qualitative resource density efficiency for workloads requiring direct hardware access and high I/O throughput. The system is suited for large-scale databases, transactional applications, data warehousing, and high-performance storage workloads. It is also appropriate for memory-intensive applications and software compilation tasks, as demonstrated by its strong performance in Passmark database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server designed for high-performance database and storage workloads. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 128 vCPUs running at 3.5 GHz, 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server delivers 75 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place this instance in the top 25% for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations, with top 10% performance in encryption and extended instruction tests. Lacking a GPU, it relies on its high-density storage and memory architecture to deliver qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive deployments. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, and high-throughput transactional applications.
